profile.summary: A variable native shrub found from coastal scrub to subalpine country throughout New Zealand. Its foliage may look grey, yellow-green or green.
profile.lookFor: Very small narrow leaves, pale and woolly underneath, on slender branchlets. Small flower heads form flat-topped clusters at the tips; mature seeds have fluffy hairs.

profile.summary: An endemic small tree of moist forest, stream margins and regenerating bush. It is widespread through both main islands, though uncommon in Central Otago.
profile.lookFor: Glossy toothed leaflets radiate from long stalks, usually in groups of five. Dark purple-black fruit forms conspicuous branched clusters.

profile.summary: An endemic compact shrub of mountain grassland and scrub in the South and Stewart islands. Its tightly pressed scale leaves make the shoots look like cords.
profile.lookFor: Short upright shoots sheathed in overlapping pairs of glossy green or olive scale leaves. Small white flowers crowd the branch tips.

profile.nameNote: Flora of New Zealand records these vernacular names. Pōhuehue is shared with other climbers, including Muehlenbeckia australis; Tororaro is also used for other Muehlenbeckia species. NZPCN recognises varieties; this species-level profile does not assign a variety to WRT’s records.
profile.summary: A native climbing or sprawling plant with many interlacing stems. It grows over other vegetation and can form dense tangled masses.
profile.lookFor: Small rounded or broadly oval leaves on wiry stems. Tiny pale flowers occur along the shoots, followed by dark seeds surrounded by pale fleshy flower parts.
